title: Life's Building Blocks
description: Necrosis claims living things are 'just goo'. Prove that every organism is built from cells — like bricks in a wall — to reclaim piece 2.

content.value: A building is made of many bricks. In the same way, the body of a living organism is made of many tiny cells. The cell is the smallest unit that can carry out all the activities of life — so it is called the basic STRUCTURAL and FUNCTIONAL unit of living things.

🧱 Bricks   → build a  🏠 House
🔵 Cells    → build a  🐘 Living body

The cell is the 'brick' of every living thing.

The cell is the 'structural unit' because it builds the body's structure, and the 'functional unit' because each cell carries out life processes — taking in food, releasing energy, growing, and getting rid of waste. Even a single cell is fully alive.

However different they look, nearly all cells share three basic parts: a CELL MEMBRANE (outer boundary), CYTOPLASM (jelly-like inside), and a NUCLEUS (control centre). You'll explore each of these in the modules ahead.
Remember two words for the cell: it's the basic STRUCTURAL unit (builds the body) and the basic FUNCTIONAL unit (does the work of living).
Key Takeaway: Cells are the building blocks of life — the basic structural and functional unit of all organisms. Nearly all cells have a cell membrane, cytoplasm and a nucleus.

quiz.question: The cell is called the basic 'structural and functional unit' of life because it…
options: builds the body AND carries out life processes
is only found in the brain
cannot do anything on its own
quiz.explain: Cells build the body (structural) and carry out living activities like getting energy (functional).

quiz.question: A living body is made of cells in the same way a house is made of…
quiz.explain: Cells are the 'bricks' that build up the body of every living organism.

quiz.question: Which three parts are found in nearly all cells?
quiz.explain: Almost every cell has a cell membrane, cytoplasm and a nucleus.
